skill.name: secret-scan
skill.description: Find leaked API keys, tokens and passwords in files, commits, history or pasted text, and stop your coding agent from writing or committing them. Use when: Check a repository and its full git history before making it public; Block commits that contain API keys with a pre-commit hook; Stop Claude Code from hardcoding a key or committing one.
skill.summary: Guide secret scanning, credential rotation, and commit protection; scanner scripts and hooks are not included.
skill.author: nexaiguy

content.user_title: Review Secret Scanning and Credential Remediation
content.value_statement: Leaked credentials can remain accessible in repository history after deletion. This guide explains scanning workflows, credential rotation, and preventive hooks, but includes no executable scanner.
actual_capabilities: Explains documented scan modes for working trees, staged changes, branch differences, history, archives, and pasted text.
Describes provider-specific detection rules, secret-looking assignments, and placeholder handling.
Shows a redacted findings example with severity, locations, fingerprints, and rotation guidance.
Outlines a remediation sequence: rotate credentials, replace literals, assess history cleanup, rescan, and add safeguards.
Documents intended pre-commit and Claude Code hook behavior, without supplying hook implementations.
Explains documented exclusions, baseline handling, and false-positive suppression options.
limitations: Only SKILL.md is included; scanner scripts, hooks, extension source, templates, and referenced remediation instructions are absent.
Advertised detection coverage, redaction, tests, and enforcement behavior cannot be verified from this guide.
The described scanner uses patterns and entropy, does not validate live credentials, and excludes binaries, large files, lockfiles, and source maps.
The documented history mode covers commits reachable from references, not stashes or the reflog.

use_cases.title: Prepare a repository for publication
use_cases.description: Plan a credential review covering current files and reachable history before making a repository public.

use_cases.title: Assess commit protection
use_cases.description: Review the documented pre-commit and agent-hook workflows before obtaining and validating a separate implementation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate credential remediation
use_cases.description: Use the rotation-first sequence to plan recovery after discovering exposed keys or passwords.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize this guide and identify which executable components are missing. Do not claim that a scan has run.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a repository review
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a secret review for my repository and reachable history. Check scanner availability first, and do not install or run missing tools.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a repository for publication.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret redacted findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these redacted findings: [findings]. Prioritize credential rotation and configuration fixes. Do not request full secrets or execute history changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: triage results from a separately verified scanner.

prompt_templates.title: Assess preventive controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess a secret-prevention rollout for [repository]. Separate documented hook behavior from verified behavior, and require approval before configuration or history changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: design controlled adoption of commit and agent safeguards.

output_examples.input: A separate scanner found a redacted API key in an old commit. What should happen next?
output: Rotate or revoke the exposed credential first.
Replace hardcoded values with environment-variable references and keep local secret files out of version control.
Assess history cleanup with backups and repository-owner approval.
Rescan the intended publication scope and verify preventive controls before publishing.

best_practices: Obtain and inspect the missing implementation before running commands or relying on protective hooks.
Keep findings redacted and rotate exposed credentials before editing code or repository history.
Back up repositories and obtain owner approval before history rewrites or mirror pushes.
anti_patterns: Assuming this guide installs or enforces the advertised scanner and hooks.
Treating deleted credentials or a clean pattern scan as proof that exposure is resolved.
Pasting full credentials into chat or broadly suppressing findings without reviewing them.

faq.question: Does this folder include a working scanner?
faq.answer: No. It contains SKILL.md only. Scanner scripts, hook implementations, extension source, and templates are explicitly excluded.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this guide?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use the guidance. The documented executable workflow requires Python 3.8 or newer and Git for repository modes.

faq.question: Does it check whether credentials are still active?
faq.answer: The described scanner does not contact providers to validate credentials. Treat credible exposure as requiring rotation.

faq.question: Are scans guaranteed to remain local?
faq.answer: The guide describes a local, network-free scanner. That claim cannot be verified because the implementation is not included.

faq.question: Does the documented history scan cover everything?
faq.answer: No. It covers commits reachable from references, excluding stashes and the reflog. Other documented exclusions include binaries and files over 2 MB.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: The guide describes line allowances, fingerprint ignores, and baselines. Review each exception, and verify support in the separately obtained implementation.
